name: Beeri
overview: Beeri was a male Hittite known in Scripture as 'the Hittite' and also referred to by the name Anah. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation as a Hittite, a people frequently mentioned in the Old Testament. The biblical texts provide limited information about him beyond these designations.
namesAndTitles: The name Beeri means '[my] cistern, well,' indicating a possible symbolic or literal connection to a source of water or provision. He is also called Anah, though the meaning of this name is not provided in the Scriptures. Both names appear in Genesis and are proper names not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Beeri is identified as the father of Judith and Dishon, though these relationships are inferred from the text. He is explicitly called the father of Zibeon and a descendant of Heth, situating him within a notable Hittite lineage. These relationships place him within a family connected to the broader narrative of the Hittite people.
scriptureSignificance: Beeri's significance lies in his role as a Hittite ancestor connected to the family of Heth, which is mentioned in the context of Israel's interactions with the Hittite people. His mention in Genesis anchors the genealogical and tribal distinctions important for understanding the peoples surrounding Israel. Although not a central figure, Beeri contributes to the biblical record of the nations and families known to the patriarchs.
